text.en:
I wish you were here, my friend carries my mono no aware toward things that were never captured and toward their disappearance—death. Here, “capture” refers not only to what escapes the camera, but also to what eludes the eye and the perception of existence itself. In the narrative of this work, the uncaptured takes the form of a spider that has left behind its web but was never seen—neither alive nor dead. Through the work, this imagined presence is rendered visible.

When looking at the web, the thought “where is (or was) the spider?” arises without intention. In that moment, existence emerges from the background: the spider’s death, disappearance, and the fragility of its being surface simultaneously. By repeatedly returning to this fictional figure, the work allows absence itself to become a perceptible and contemplative condition.

The project is structured by a set of twelve-sided dice rules written by AI. The AI provides prompts—rules for producing fictional photographs of the spider and its web. Through rolling the dice and interpreting these prompts, which embed different photographic processes and technical procedures, I photograph, process, generate, and modify images related to the spider and the web.

Installed at Beaconsfield Gallery in a deliberately unorderly manner, images produced through disparate photographic methods are dispersed across the space, quietly linked by the imagined presence of the spider. A video unfolds slowly as a lament for this fictional friend, while the dice rules are displayed on a table. Rules, play, and nostalgia intertwine within the site, forming a ground that holds emotion, thought, and imagination. The work prepares itself for an emerging technological era, while simultaneously sounding echoes for nostalgia that is constantly slipping into the past, and for the fragility that inhabits absence.
text.cn:
《I wish you were here, my friend》 寄托了我对未被捕捉之物及其消逝（死亡）的物哀之情。这里的“未被捕捉”（capture）既指镜头所未能记录的、眼睛未曾看见的，也指未被确证与感知的存在。在作品的叙事中，这一未被捕捉之物是一只只留下蛛网、却从未被发现过的蜘蛛——无论其生，亦或其死，作品都将对它的想象加以视觉化。

当凝视蛛网，思绪无端地浮现出“蜘蛛在哪（或曾在哪）”这一问题时，存在从其背景中显现出来；蜘蛛的死亡、消逝，与其存在本身的脆弱性一并涌现。作品通过对这一虚构对象的反复召回，使缺席本身成为可以被感知与思考的状态。

整个项目被置于一套由人工智能编写的十二面骰子规则之中：AI 为我提供“如何制作关于蜘蛛／蛛网的虚构照片”的规则（prompt），而我则通过掷骰并理解、执行这些包含不同摄影流程与技术制作手段的规则，去拍摄、处理、生成与修改关于蜘蛛与蛛网的图像。

在 Beaconsfield Gallery 的呈现中，作品以一种并不规整的方式展开。不同摄影方法生成的图像在空间中彼此并置，却被这只虚构的蜘蛛悄然串联；录像以缓慢的节奏道出对这一虚构朋友的哀思，十二面骰子的规则被陈列于台面之上。规则、游戏与乡愁在场域中纠缠，成为承载我情绪、思绪与想象的温床——作品既是在为一个崭新的技术时代做准备，也是在为不断滑入过去的乡愁，以及空白之处的脆弱，敲响回声。
text.tw:
在這個項目中，我試圖通過視覺線索重建記憶的碎片化。圖像充當錨點，抓住那些不斷流逝的時刻。

這個過程涉及多重曝光的疊加和對膠片的物理處理，以創造一種衰敗與重生的感覺。
